answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, slashable collateral rather than the number of agent identities. Each agent locks a deposit, and the protocol lets other participants challenge a suspicious cluster; if an audit proves those identities share control or fabricated activity, their deposits are slashed and their voting weight removed. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to fund every identity and risk losing capital, so multiplying lotus, plume, and relic accounts becomes expensive rather than free.
